dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24; dhāraṇā 82 = verses 105–106 and dhāraṇā 89 = verses 113–114, otherwise one verse each; dhāraṇā 112 = verse 137)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: jñānaprakāśakaṃ sarvaṃ sarveṇātmā prakāśakaḥ | ekam ekasvabhāvatvāj jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ vibhāvyate ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, compared with Wallis's concordance, Pradīpaka and the Singh scan
sanskrit_variants: verse 137: Sandhi corrected: GRETIL -svabhāvatvāt jñānaṃ; Wallis and Pradīpaka -svabhāvatvāj jñānaṃ. Singh reports a second reading current in the Śaiva tradition (per Lakshmanjoo): jñānaṃ prakāśakaṃ loke ātmā caiva prakāśakaḥ | anayor apṛthagbhāvāj jñāne jñānī vibhāvyate; Wallis prints the GRETIL text but his translation follows this second reading.
dharana.rendering: Everything is revealed by knowing, and the Self is revealed by everything; because their nature is one, knowing and the known are contemplated as one.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh: 'knowing' here stands for the knower; the known is revealed by the knower and the knower by the known. He cites the Ucchuṣmabhairava ('so long as there are no knowers, how can there be the known?') and a verse quoted by Śivopādhyāya: manifestation is not separate from the light of consciousness, nor that light from I-consciousness. Contemplating subject, object and consciousness as one reality, one attains Bhairava's nature. Singh classes it as śāktopāya. Singh reports a second reading, per Lakshmanjoo: 'knowledge reveals things in the world and the Self is the source of all revelation; since they are not different, the knower is revealed in knowledge'. Wallis's translation follows that reading.
dharana.instruction: Notice that what you know and the one who knows reveal each other, and rest in them as one knowing.

numbering_variants.mystery_within_parallel: The parallel-translations section of The Mystery Within labels verse 137 'Dharana 114', because from verse 106 on it gives every verse its own number (106 = 83 … 137 = 114). Singh and the same book's Session Two list put this at dhāraṇā 112. Not followed.

source_disagreements: Verse 137: Singh reports a second reading current in the Śaiva tradition (per Lakshmanjoo), jñānaṃ prakāśakaṃ loke ātmā caiva prakāśakaḥ | anayor apṛthagbhāvāj jñāne jñānī vibhāvyate; Wallis prints the standard text but translates the second reading. The paraphrase follows the printed text; both readings arrive at knower and knowing as one.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 137 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

points: knowing, which is the same nature in both
geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is the knower and the known as two faces of one knowing, each revealing the other.
geometry.svg_hint: two facing arcs that join into a single circle
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: One knowing
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: the split between the one who knows and what is known closes into a single knowing. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: wherever the breath naturally ends; this door places nothing on the breath
breath.cue: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps you settle, then let the count go. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Turn attention toward what the verse names, and let everything else stay in the background
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: The knower and the known, each revealing the other

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: Everything is revealed by knowing, and the Self is revealed by everything; because their nature is one, knowing and the known are contemplated as one.
adiyogi.method_summary: Look at, or listen to, anything. Notice that it is revealed by your knowing, and that your knowing is revealed by it. Let the two be seen as one nature, one knowing, and rest there.

honesty.disclosure: Door 112 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 112 (verse 137) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. legacy.disclosure: Vijnana Bhairava Tantra. The [retired posture]–verse pairing on this door is a School of 112 Doorways device (school_device), not a claim of ancient one-to-one canon. Lotus is an optional seat, not proof of mastery.
legacy.notes: Teaching reference, marked historical and observe_only: not a class drill, and no readiness flag promotes it into one. Verse 138 is yukti 112 in the usual counting of the Vijnana Bhairava Tantra, the last of the 112 brief instructions. It points toward a settling in which restless mind, breath-as-effort, the feeling of being a separate knower, and the self-image are no longer being held in place. This gloss is not a translation and not a technique for forcing that settling. Verse 49's heart-lotus is a cousin image; this door does not collapse the two into one claim. The [retired posture] is never the method.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. If this becomes abstract, simply rest in plain seeing or hearing. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.

notes: Never force [retired posture]. Knee cartilage does not negotiate. If either knee lifts high, complains, or the foot must be hauled into place, come out at once.
Prior knee injury, knee surgery, ligament sprain, or pain under the kneecap: do not attempt lotus. A chair, or an easy seat in which both knees are comfortable, is the door for that day.
Ankle sprain, Achilles pain, or hips that do not already externally rotate: same rule. The hips lead. The ankles are not levers.
Hip replacement, or any limit a physician has set on hip rotation: stay inside that limit. This text is not a clearance to [retired posture] the leg.
Pregnancy: lotus is optional and often uncomfortable. Leave for numbness, pubic pain, or breath that cannot deepen. Side-sitting or a bolster is enough.
Sciatica or pain that travels down the leg: do not [retired posture] the legs into a shape that reproduces it.
Numbness in a foot is a reason to leave immediately, not a sign of progress.
